title: /resources hub newest-first surfacing of the new post has no test (acceptance criterion, NONE coverage)
evidence:
resources_view.gleam view_rent_data():
          html.div(
            [attribute.class("mt-6 grid sm:grid-cols-2 gap-6")],
            posts
              |> list.sort(fn(a, b) {
                string.compare(b.published_iso, a.published_iso)
              })
              |> list.map(rent_card),

Acceptance criterion (diff spec): "appears in sitemap.xml + /resources hub newest-first". grep of server/test/ and .pi/skills/bug-hunt/scenarios/ for "rent-data|resources/dublin|newest" returns no test asserting the hub section, its card list, or its ordering; the only resources_view assertions in content_test.gleam are consent/tracking-snippet checks.
detail: The hub's newest-first ordering is enforced only by this untested list.sort. With Q2 added, ordering is observable for the first time; a dropped or inverted sort would ship a stale quarter leading the hub, undetected.
recommended_fix: Add a unit test rendering resources_view and pinning card order — Q2's slug/href precedes Q1's — so a dropped or inverted sort fails the suite.

title: Per-post rent-post view invariants (cap/CPI derivation, FAQ-schema parity, NewsArticle datePublished) rendered only for Q1, not the new Q2 post (PARTIAL)
detail: Shared view code is covered via Q1, but Q2's own rendered instances — e.g. datePublished "2026-08-24" and the rpz freshness line on the Q2 page — are never asserted; a Q2-copy regression would pass unnoticed.
recommended_fix: Generalise like the sibling iteration tests: list.each(rent_post.posts, ...) asserting rpz.cpi strings, FAQ fragment count >= 2, and each post's own datePublished, plus add Q2 to the snippets page list.
